MODULE 2: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

4-ON-4 DEFENSIVE SHUTDOWN

20 MIN BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

#### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of four. Make sure each basket has a minimum of three teams and a maximum of six. Teams will play continuous half-court 4-on-4 with additional teams waiting at the half-court area. If a defensive stop is secured (defensive rebound or forced turnover), the defense gets 2 points and stays on defense while a new offense comes on from the half-court area (the old offense team rotates off to the end of the line). If the offense scores, they rotate to defense and play against a new team on offense (the old defense team rotates off to the end of the line).

#### SCORING

Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound or forced turnover).

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Pressuring the ball with intensity
- Helping and stopping the ball
- Disrupting the offense with double teams

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- The defense must always ensure there is adequate ball pressure: the on-ball defender must be within arm's distance from the offensive player.
- The defense must avoid fouling.
- The defense achieves an extra 2 points for any successful trap (double team) which leads to a turnover.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Send off defense when lapses happen (inadequate ball pressure, foul, etc.).
- Emphasize and teach defensive concepts and philosophy.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "What does good ball pressure look like?"
- "What are the best scenarios to trap?"

MODULE 2: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

5-ON-5 LOADS-BASED

20 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

#### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of five players, based on the number of courts available. Try to have a maximum of five teams on each full-court. In instances of very high numbers, half-courts can be used. Teams play to three baskets. After a team scores three baskets, they get 1 point. The losing team will rotate off while the next team waiting rotates on. The game is then continually played, with teams keeping track of their total number of points over the course of the activity.

#### SCORING

3 baskets = 1 point for team.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Maintaining good spacing
- Hunting out open shots

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How can you get the most efficient shot?"
- "How can we help teammates emphasize continuous ball pressure?"
- "What can you do to space the floor effectively?"

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Play 4-on-4, with a +1 who is always on offense.
- For younger players, the lava is the paint area. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line).
- Escape the lava. After a pass or cut is completed, the offensive player without the ball has three seconds to escape the lava (space out outside the 3PT line). If they are still inside after three seconds, a turnover is called.
- Pass and cut is a turnover. Players can only create an advantage through a static 1-on-1 where the ball-handler creates an advantage with a dribble move from the perimeter, or through a post-up. Teammates should maintain spacing (following the 'lava' load), ready to receive the ball.
- Double teams that lead to turnovers result in an extra 3 points.
- No ball pressure results in the defensive team losing 1 point and the offense regaining possession on the sideline.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Organize the waiting teams on the sideline so teams transition quickly for the next repetition.
- Ensure players substitute every few minutes.
- Emphasize and teach offensive and defensive concepts and philosophy.

FINAL BUZZER

Basketball School

## FINAL BUZZER

is our closing huddle where coaches see the players off as a group. The Final Buzzer should take no more than 5 minutes to maximize player's attention spans. There are five parts that should be covered in every Final Buzzer:

CALL IN

Players are verbally called in to huddle up and stand in a circle with all players and coaches if numbers allow (for larger groups, coaches may need to stand in front of the players).

CONNECTIONS

Players are given connections by the coaches as they join the Tip-Off (example of connections: high five, fist bump, handshake, pat on the shoulder).

COMMUNICATIONS

Players are delivered any relevant news or information for the day. This can include rules, expectations, directions to the bathroom, expectations for water break, etc.

CONCLUSION

Players are debriefed on the learnings and prepared for the end of the module.

CHEER

Players and coaches give an enthusiastic and excited cheer together!

CONNECTIONS

MODULE 3: FULL OUTLINE

WARM UP

Basketball School

TAIL TAG

10 MIN
BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available space (no baskets needed)

### EQUIPMENT

1 bib per player

### DESCRIPTION

Players tuck bibs (tails) into the back of their shorts. Players spend 90 seconds attempting to pull as many other tails as they can, without having their own taken. When a tail is taken, it is immediately thrown back to the player to continue playing.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Play the same game while dribbling.
- Players must link arms with a teammate. They must work in a small chain to pull the tails from other teams.
- Players work in groups of four and play 2-on-2 in a small space while dribbling. One team wins when they get both opposing players out.

### SCORING

N/A

### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure no bibs remain on the floor. When a bib is pulled, it must be given back to the player immediately and worn again.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Developing agility
- Developing ball manipulation skills

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- How could you better protect your tail from your opponents?

MODULE 3: FULL OUTLINE

WARM UP

Basketball School

TEAM TAG

10 MIN
BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available space (no baskets needed). Different groups inside half-court areas.

### EQUIPMENT

None needed. Can add 1 ball for dribbling loads.

### DESCRIPTION

Players will be divided into teams consisting of anywhere between four and 10 players. One team will start as the escapers inside the half-court boundaries, while the other team will start as the taggers and stand in a line on the baseline. When the first tagger runs out and attempts to tag one of the escapers, the coach starts recording time on a stopwatch. The moment an escaper is tagged, they must stand out on the sideline, while the tagger sprints back to hi-five the next tagger who can start to run out. Time stops when all the escapers are tagged. Both teams then change roles, with the other team attempting to beat the first team's time to win the game.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Play in a smaller space, e.g. inside the 3PT line
- Play the same game dribbling
- Only dribble with the left hand

### STAFF ROLE

- Time each round on stopwatch.
- Tell the players what team wins each round.
- Make sure taggers hi-five their teammates before they start running out.

### SCORING

Team with the fastest time wins

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- How can you be a great teammate on the sideline to support your team?

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Developing agility
- Competing in teams
- Developing ball manipulation skills

Load for younger players
